Let's reconsider the question carefully.

The question is: "What happens if you clean your house on New Year's Day?"

The options are:

A. Nothing happens if you clean your house on New Year's Day.

B. You will be unlucky for the rest of the year.

C. You will be lucky for the rest of the year.

D. You will sweep out all of the good luck.

In many cultural traditions, especially in East Asian cultures, it is believed that cleaning on New Year's Day is bad luck because it "sweeps away" the good luck and fortune that has just arrived with the new year. This is why people avoid cleaning on that day.

Option D says: "You will sweep out all of the good luck." This matches the superstition that cleaning on New Year's Day sweeps away good luck.

Option B says: "You will be unlucky for the rest of the year." This is a consequence of sweeping out good luck, but it's more general.

Option A says: "Nothing happens if you clean your house on New Year's Day." This is a neutral statement, but it ignores the superstition.

Option C says: "You will be lucky for the rest of the year." This contradicts the superstition.

Between B and D, D is more precise and directly reflects the superstition.

Therefore, the correct answer is D.

Answer: D
